intervals.label: STCF project (proposed 2011; Hefei named as the site in the project documents)
intervals.note: Start = the month the STCF was proposed (2011.12); the facility record starts with the project because the proposed collider and its experiment start then. The documents name Hefei as the host: the Anhui and Hefei governments launched the key-technology R&D in April 2022 ('Government of Anhui Province and Hefei City Launch the STCF Key Technology R&D', Zheng 2024), and the host city is not dated earlier in the sources fetched. Proposed, not approved.
intervals.quote: Proposed at “workshop for acc. Based high energy physics development strategy”

name: Super Tau-Charm Facility site, Hefei (proposed)
notes: A project-level facility: the proposed STCF is not built; there is no operating laboratory yet. It exists so that the proposed collider, its experiment and its area marker have a host; its lead institution is the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC).

operator_text.note: The talks call the project leadership the 'USTC Leading Group'; no operator exists until the facility is approved and built.
operator_text.value: University of Science and Technology of China (leads the project)

summary.plain: The proposed home of China's Super Tau-Charm Facility, an electron-positron collider planned for the Future Big Science City of Hefei and led by the University of Science and Technology of China. It has not been approved or built.
summary.technical: STCF project site in Hefei, Anhui: Future Big Science City, about 1 km², three candidate sites under geological exploration; Anhui, Hefei and USTC fund the key-technology R&D (364 M CNY) from 2023; construction proposed for the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030).
